structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single CANDIDATE pre-Python architecture design document for event ingress at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/event-ingress.md, using the supplied authority and local evidence, without implementation, source/config/test changes, EOS edits, service changes, secrets exposure, or implicit Founder approval.
structuredContent.summary: The work packet has a coherent documentation-only outcome: synthesize existing Founder-approved architecture direction, pre-Python gate rows G13-G15, Node behavioral evidence, and EOS constraints into one reviewable candidate design artifact covering direct webhook and outbound relay ingress, internal event contract semantics, auth/profile selection, identity/correlation/deduplication/reordering/replay, durable effects, crash boundaries, and no-polling constraints. It explicitly limits authority to candidate design drafting and recording unresolved Founder decisions rather than adopting new architecture.
implementation_unknowns: Exact contents and locations of the cited local evidence must be found during implementation, including authority section references, bin/alienintent.mjs, dispatcher behavior, GitHub authority tests, Issue1 replay proof, B-DISP D10, and any packet/readiness evidence conventions.
The writer must determine how the repository’s existing documentation style, packet structure, source/invariant mapping format, and documentation checker expectations are represented locally.
The document author must reconcile cited historical Node evidence with candidate Python-facing architecture without overstating it as Python capability proof or adopted stable API.
The author must identify any genuinely unresolved Founder decisions encountered while drafting and present them as candidate questions/options rather than silently deciding them.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable against the requested artifact and source mapping: reviewers can inspect that only the allowed documentation/packet paths changed, that the design is labelled CANDIDATE, that G13-G15 are covered, that polling and network exactly-once claims are excluded, that direct webhook and outbound relay share a profile-scoped ingress contract, that examples include success and failure cases, that crash boundaries around persist/ack/effect are enumerated, and that unresolved Founder decisions are explicitly recorded. One independent content review is meaningful because the output is a bounded design document with traceable evidence references, not a coupled implementation requiring multi-system runtime validation.
material_risks: The document could accidentally invent or adopt architecture beyond the supplied authority instead of labelling material semantics as candidate for Founder review.
The writer could overclaim historical Node/live Issue1 evidence as fresh verification, Python capability proof, or stable API authority.
Cross-document dependencies may tempt implicit adoption of neighboring candidate documents; the packet requires unresolved cross-document choices to be recorded rather than assumed.
Security/authentication/profile-selection language may create material trust-boundary implications and must be framed as candidate design where not already Founder-approved.
The no-polling rule and relay replay semantics must be stated carefully so bounded retries are not disguised as polling and durable replay is not misrepresented as exactly-once network delivery.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed with drafting the single candidate design document and any authorized local packet/readiness evidence, using traceable source/invariant mapping and recording rather than resolving any material Founder decisions that arise.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the supplied task establishes a clear, bounded, documentation-only objective; identifies the governing architecture authority and exclusions; supplies enough acceptance criteria for independent review; and explicitly authorizes readiness assessment and candidate drafting while withholding implementation approval. Remaining uncertainty is ordinary engineering/documentation research about locating and synthesizing local evidence, not unresolved owner intent. The event-ingress, no-polling, and internal event semantics concerns are tightly coupled around one ingress design artifact, so splitting would reduce coherence rather than isolate independent decisions.
